newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel takes security precautions for holiday.
newsitem.headline: Israel takes security precautions for holiday.

text.p: Security forces are throwing protective rings around Israeli cities which plan to go ahead with street carnivals for Purim holiday on Sunday in spite of a deadly bomb attack and threats of more to come.
Police said roadblocks would go up at entrances to cities in Israel's heavily populated central region. Thousands of officers and civilian volunteers would patrol the streets.

The Moslem extremist group Hamas, which claimed responsibility for killing three Israeli women in Friday's suicide bombing of a Tel Aviv cafe, threatened on Saturday at launch further attacks if building continued for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"The persistence of the Zionists to build the dirty settlement on Jabal Abu Ghneim will compel us to continue our attacks, striking against the Zionists," said a statement faxed to an international news agency by Hamas' military wing.

Israel's groundbreaking on Tuesday for a project to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a pine-covered hill between Jerusalem and the West Bank town of Bethlehem, occupied in the 1967 Middle East War, drew international condemnation and Palestinian rage.

Fierce Israeli-Arab clashes flared in the West Bank town of Hebron on Saturday for the second straight day. Israeli soldiers fired live ammunition, rubber bullets and teargas at hundreds of Arab protesters who threw petrol bombs and rocks.
Hospital officials said at least 20 Palestinians suffered gunshot wounds. The Israeli army said soldiers fired live ammunition "when their lives were in danger".
Another 80 Arabs were treated for other injuries or teargas inhalation in some of the most serious Israeli-Palestinian violence in months, the officials said.
One protester lost an eye but no deaths were reported.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to press ahead with the settlement at the East Jerusalem site Israel calls Har Homa, angrily rejecting Palestinian allegations his right-wing government brought Friday's bombing upon itself.
An anonymous caller to Israeli police on Friday said Hamas claimed responsibility for the suicide attack. The faxed statement on Saturday referred to the bombing as "a wonderful martyrdom operation".
The mayors of Tel Aviv, Haifa and Ramat Gan said on Israel Radio they had not cancelled plans for Purim street carnivals on Sunday because doing so would be giving in to terrorism.
"But I will understand if parents want to keep their children home," Ramat Gan mayor Zvi Bar said.
The festival celebrates the Jews' delivery from genocide in ancient Persia.
Tel Aviv planned a "Dizengoff is laughing" carnival on Dizengoff street, where suicide bombers struck a year ago during the Purim holiday, killing 13 people.
For some families, there was little joy. The three women killed in Friday's blast were to be buried on Sunday.
